topic.title: we don't need anything
topic.claim: When your parents say 'we don't need anything', they mean 'don't make us your expense.'
topic.moment: You ask what they want for their anniversary and they say, again, 'nothing beta, we have everything.'

turn.believed: They're being humble, or they genuinely can't think of anything.
turn.actually: They're refusing to become a line item in the life they spent everything building for you.

topic.because: They were the providers your whole life. Needing from you flips a thing they're not ready to flip. 'Nothing' is how pride survives dependence.
topic.payoff: 'We don't need anything' was never about the gift. It was them trying to stay the ones who give.
topic.feeling: the ache of love that won't let itself be looked after
topic.villain: the one-way direction care is supposed to flow in a family
topic.behaviour: parents deflect every offer, insist they're fine, hide what they'd actually like
topic.mechanism: accepting from their child reverses the provider role they built their identity on, so they say no to protect it
topic.group: adults who want to spend on parents who won't let them
topic.send_to: a friend stuck on what to buy parents who 'need nothing'
topic.why_now: gifting season when the 'what do you want' call happens weekly
